items.followUp: What was the main idea of Rutherford’s nuclear model of the atom?

rubric.why: The model describes electrons embedded in positively charged matter.
rubric.description: Describes the atom as a positively charged sphere or matter with electrons embedded in it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere or matter.

rubric.why: J. J. Thomson proposed the plum pudding theory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming J. J. Thomson.

modelAnswer: The plum pudding theory describes the atom as a positively charged sphere with electrons embedded in it, like plums in a pudding.
It was proposed by J. J. Thomson.

items.followUp: Why does the shielding effect increase down a group?

rubric.why: Electrons in inner shells cause the shielding effect.
rubric.description: Identifies the electrons responsible for shielding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that inner-shell electrons cause shielding.

rubric.why: Inner-shell electrons screen outer-shell electrons from the nucleus, reducing the attraction between them.
rubric.description: Explains how shielding affects the attraction between the nucleus and outer-shell electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that inner-shell electrons screen outer-shell electrons from the nucleus or reduce the attraction between them.

modelAnswer: The shielding effect is the reduction in attraction between the nucleus and outer-shell electrons caused by inner-shell electrons.
Inner-shell electrons screen the outer-shell electrons from the nuclear charge.

items.followUp: Write any two properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: Low melting and boiling points are characteristic of many covalent compounds.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds have a low melting point or low boiling point.

rubric.why: Covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity because they lack mobile charged particles.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds are poor electrical conductors or do not conduct electricity.

modelAnswer: Covalent compounds usually have low melting and boiling points.
They are generally poor conductors of electricity.
